action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). </commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>

</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>

user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.\nDaisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"\nAssistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.\nDaisy: "Please review PR #1234"\nAssistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.\nDaisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"\nAssistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:

- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

1	/*

     6	 */
     7	import React from 'react'
     8	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
     9	import {FormattedMessage, FormattedNumber} from 'react-intl'
    10	import {
    11	    Stack,
    12	    Text,
    13	    useBreakpointValue
    14	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
    15	import {useItemVariant} from '.'
    16	import {getPriceData} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils'
    17	import DisplayPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price'
    18	
    19	const PricePerItem = ({currency, basePrice}) => {
    20	    return (
    21	        <Text fontSize={{base: '12px', lg: '14px'}}>
    22	            <FormattedNumber style="currency" currency={currency} value={basePrice} />
    23	            <FormattedMessage
    24	                defaultMessage="ea"
    25	                id="price_per_item.label.each"
    26	                description="Abbreviated 'each', follows price per item, like $10/ea"
    27	            />
    28	        </Text>
    29	    )
    30	}
    31	
    32	PricePerItem.propTypes = {
    33	    currency: PropTypes.string.isRequired,
    34	    basePrice: PropTypes.number
    35	}
    36	
    37	/**
    38	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
    39	 * pricing, taking into account applied discounts as well as base item prices.
    40	 */
    41	const ItemPrice = ({currency, align = 'right', baseDirection = 'column', ...props}) => {
    42	    const variant = useItemVariant()
    43	    const {price, priceAfterItemDiscount} = variant
    44	    const isASet = variant?.type?.set
    45	    const isMaster = variant?.type?.master
    46	    let priceData
    47	    // When variant has basket pricing, we should prioritize these prices for displaying
    48	    // since they may have take promotion/discount into account
    49	    // NOTE: try NOT to re-calculate these values since basket-level discount is complicated
    50	    if (variant?.itemId) {
    51	        priceData = {
    52	            currentPrice: priceAfterItemDiscount,
    53	            // we don't want to show strikethrough price for cart since listPrice is not available via basket pricing
    54	            listPrice: null,
    55	            pricePerUnit: variant?.pricePerUnit,
    56	            isASet,
    57	            isMaster,
    58	            isRange: isASet || isMaster || false,
    59	            isOnSale: price > priceAfterItemDiscount
    60	        }
    61	    } else {
    62	        // for wishlist page we extract price info from variant/product obj
    63	        priceData = getPriceData(variant)
    64	    }
    65	    const isDesktop = useBreakpointValue({base: false, lg: true})
    66	
    67	    return (
    68	        <Stack
    69	            textAlign={align}
    70	            direction={baseDirection}
    71	            justifyContent={align === 'left' ? 'flex-start' : 'flex-end'}
    72	            alignItems="baseline"
    73	            spacing={priceData?.isOnSale ? 0 : 1}
    74	            wrap="nowrap"
    75	            {...props}
    76	        >
    77	            {!isDesktop && variant?.quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (
    78	                <PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />
    79	            )}
    80	
    81	            {variant?.itemId ? (
    82	                <DisplayPrice
    83	                    labelForA11y={variant?.name}
    84	                    currency={currency}

   286	                        {basket.shippingTotal === 0 ? (
   287	                            <Text
   288	                                as="span"
   289	                                color="green.700"
   290	                                textTransform="uppercase"
   291	                                fontSize={fontSize}
   292	                            >

   299	                            <Text fontSize={fontSize}>

   306	                        ) : (
   307	                            <Text fontSize={fontSize} color="gray.700">

    10	/**
    11	 * Get the human-friendly version of the variation values that users have selected.
    12	 * Useful for displaying these values in the UI.
    13	 *
    14	 * @param {Object} variationAttributes - The products variation attributes.
    15	 * @param {Object} values - The variations selected attribute values.
    16	 * @returns {Object} - A key value map of the display name and display value.
    17	 *
    18	 * @example
    19	 * const displayValues = getDisplayVariationValues(
    20	 *     [ { "id": "color", "name": "Colour", "values": [ { "name": "royal", "orderable": true, "value": "JJ5FUXX" } ] } ],
    21	 *     { "color": "JJ5FUXX" }
    22	 * )
    23	 * // returns { "Colour": "royal" }
    24	 */
    25	export const getDisplayVariationValues = (variationAttributes, values = {}) => {
    26	    if (!variationAttributes || !Array.isArray(variationAttributes)) {
    27	        return {}
    28	    }
    29	
    30	    const returnVal = Object.entries(values).reduce((acc, [id, value]) => {
    31	        const attribute = variationAttributes.find(({id: attributeId}) => attributeId === id)
    32	        if (!attribute || !attribute.values) {
    33	            return acc
    34	        }
    35	
    36	        const attributeValue = attribute.values.find(
    37	            ({value: attributeValue}) => attributeValue === value
    38	        )
    39	
    40	        if (attributeValue) {
    41	            return {
    42	                ...acc,
    43	                [attribute.name]: attributeValue.name
    44	            }
    45	        }
    46	        return acc
    47	    }, {})
    48	    return returnVal
    49	}

    51	/**
    52	 * Normalizes data for product sets and product bundles into the same format
    53	 * Useful for operations that apply to both product sets and product bundles
    54	 * Creates deep clones of child products to avoid mutation issues
    55	 *
    56	 * @param {Object} product - A product set or product bundle
    57	 * @returns {Object} - returns normalized product if product is a set/bundle, otherwise returns original product
    58	 */
    59	export const normalizeSetBundleProduct = (product) => {
    60	    if (!product?.type.set && !product?.type.bundle) return product
    61	
    62	    const childProducts = product?.type.set
    63	        ? product.setProducts.map((child) => {
    64	              return {
    65	                  product: {...child},
    66	                  quantity: null
    67	              }
    68	          })
    69	        : product.bundledProducts.map((child) => {
    70	              return {
    71	                  ...child,
    72	                  product: {...child.product}
    73	              }
    74	          })
    75	
    76	    return {
    77	        ...product,
    78	        childProducts
    79	    }

    92	    const itemsToBeUpdated = []
    93	    bundle?.bundledProductItems?.forEach((bundleChild) => {
    94	        const childSelection = childProductSelections?.find(
    95	            (childProduct) =>

   103	        if (childSelection && selectedProductId !== bundleChild.productId) {

   106	                productId: selectedProductId,
   107	                quantity: childSelection.quantity ?? bundleChild.quantity

   114	/**

   116	 * If a product is a master,
   117	 *  currentPrice: get the lowest price (including promotional prices) among variants
   118	 *  listPrice: get the list price of the variant that has lowest price (including promotional price)
   119	 *  maxPrice: the max price in tieredPrices of variant that has lowest price
   120	 * @param {object} product - product detail object
   121	 * @param {object} opts - options to pass into the function like intl, quantity, and currency
   122	 */
   123	export const getPriceData = (product, opts = {}) => {
   124	    const {quantity = 1} = opts
   125	    const isASet = product?.hitType === 'set' || !!product?.type?.set
   126	    const isMaster = product?.hitType === 'master' || !!product?.type?.master
   127	    let currentPrice
   128	    let variantWithLowestPrice
   129	    // grab the variant that has the lowest price (including promotional price)
   130	    if (isMaster) {
   131	        variantWithLowestPrice = findLowestPrice(product)
   132	        currentPrice = variantWithLowestPrice?.minPrice
   133	    } else {
   134	        currentPrice = findLowestPrice(product)?.minPrice
   135	    }
   136	
   137	    // since the price is the lowest value among price books, each product will have at lease a single item tiered price at quantity 1
   138	    // the highest value of tieredPrices is presumptively the list price
   139	    const tieredPrices = variantWithLowestPrice?.data?.tieredPrices || product?.tieredPrices || []

   141	        ? Math.max(...tieredPrices.map((item) => item.price))
   142	        : undefined

   144	    const listPrice = highestTieredPrice?.price

   147	    const filteredTiered = tieredPrices.filter((tiered) => tiered.quantity <= quantity)

   150	        filteredTiered.reduce((prev, curr) => {
   151	            return Math.abs(curr.quantity - quantity) < Math.abs(prev.quantity - quantity)
   152	                ? curr
   153	                : prev
   154	        })

   157	        listPrice,
   158	        pricePerUnit: product?.pricePerUnit,
   159	        isOnSale: currentPrice < listPrice,
   160	        isASet,
   161	        isMaster,

   165	        isRange: (isMaster && product?.variants?.length > 1) || isASet || false,

   167	        tieredPrice: closestTieredPrice?.price,
   168	        maxPrice: product?.priceMax || maxTieredPrice
   169	    }
   170	}

   182	export const filterImageGroups = (imageGroups = [], filters) => {
   183	    if (!filters) {

   185	    }

   187	    const {viewType, variationValues = {}} = filters

   195	        !!selectedAttributeId && !!selectedAttributeValue

   197	                  variationAttributes.some(

   211	 *
   212	 * @param {Product} product
   213	 * @param {object} opts
   214	 * @param {string} opts.swatchViewType - The `viewTypeId` for the swatch image. Defaults to `swatch`.

   216	 * @returns {VariationAttributes[]} decoratedVariationAttributes

   221	    return product?.variationAttributes?.map((variationAttribute) => ({
   222	        ...variationAttribute,
   223	        values: variationAttribute.values.map((value) => {
   224	            const variationValues = {[variationAttribute.id]: value.value}
   225	
   226	            return {
   227	                ...value,
   228	                swatch: filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups, {
   229	                    viewType: swatchViewType,
   230	                    variationValues
   231	                })?.[0]?.images[0],
   232	                href: rebuildPathWithParams(
   233	                    productUrlBuilder({id: product.productId}),
   234	                    variationValues
   235	                )
   236	            }
   237	        })
   238	    }))
   239	}
   240	
   241	/**
   242	 * Find the lowest price of a product, across all of its price books and promotions
   243	 * @param {Object} product - product data from the API
   244	 * @returns {Object|undefined} the lowest price for the given product. If it's a promotional price, the promotion will also be returned.
   245	 */
   246	export const findLowestPrice = (product) => {
   247	    if (!product) return
   248	
   249	    // Look at all of the variants, only if it's a master product.
   250	    // i.e. when a shopper has narrowed down to a variant, do not look into other variants
   251	    const isMaster = product.hitType === 'master' || !!product.type?.master
   252	    if (isMaster && !product.variants) {
   253	        console.warn(
   254	            'Expecting `product.variants` to exist. For more accuracy, please tweak your API request to ask for the variants details.'
   255	        )
   256	    }
   257	    const array = isMaster && product.variants ? product.variants : [product]
   258	
   259	    const res = array.reduce(
   260	        (prev, data) => {
   261	            const promotions = data.productPromotions || []
   262	            const [smallestPromotionalPrice, promo] = getSmallestValByProperty(
   263	                promotions,
   264	                'promotionalPrice'
   265	            )
   266	
   267	            let salePrice = data.price
   268	            let promotion = null
   269	            if (smallestPromotionalPrice && smallestPromotionalPrice < data.price) {
   270	                salePrice = smallestPromotionalPrice
   271	                promotion = promo
   272	            }
   273	
   274	            return salePrice < prev.minPrice ? {minPrice: salePrice, promotion, data} : prev
   275	        },
   276	        {minPrice: Infinity, promotion: null, data: null}
   277	    )
   278	    return {
   279	        ...res,
   280	        // when minPrice is infinity, meaning there is no variant with lowest price found, we rest the value to 0 as minPrice to be able to use this value on UI

   291	 */
   292	const getSmallestValByProperty = (arr, key) => {

   294	    if (!key) {
   295	        throw new Error('Please specify a key.')
   296	    }
   297	    const filtered = arr.filter((item) => {
   298	        const value = item[key]
   299	        return value === 0 || value === '0' ? true : Number(value)
   300	    })
   301	    if (filtered.length === 0) return []
   302	
   303	    return filtered.reduce(
   304	        (prev, item) => {
   305	            const value = item[key]
   306	            const [prevValue] = prev
   307	            return value < prevValue ? [value, item] : prev
   308	        },
   309	        [Infinity, null]
   310	    )
   311	}

    14	/**

    17	 *      on PLP, Show From X where X is the lowest of its children
    18	 *      on PDP, Show From X where X is the lowest of its children and
    19	 *          the set children will have it own price as From X (cross) Y
    20	 * // if a product is a master
    21	 *      on PLP and PDP, show From X (cross) Y , the X and Y are
    22	 *          current and list price of variant that has the lowest price (including promotionalPrice)
    23	 * // if a standard/bundle

    25	 * @param currency - currency
    26	 * @param quantity - quantity to take into the account for price display
    27	 * @param currentPriceProps - extra props to be passing to CurrentPrice component
    28	 * @param listPriceProps - extra props to be passing to ListPrice component
    29	 * @param labelForA11y - label to be used for a11y
    30	 */
    31	const DisplayPrice = ({
    32	    labelForA11y,
    33	    priceData,
    34	    currency,
    35	    quantity = 1,
    36	    currentPriceProps = {},
    37	    listPriceProps = {}
    38	}) => {
    39	    const {listPrice, currentPrice, isASet, isMaster, isOnSale, isRange} = priceData
    40	    const renderCurrentPrice = (isRange) => (
    41	        <CurrentPrice
    42	            labelForA11y={labelForA11y}
    43	            price={currentPrice * quantity}
    44	            as="b"
    45	            currency={currency}
    46	            isRange={isRange}
    47	            {...currentPriceProps}
    48	        />
    49	    )
    50	
    51	    const renderListPrice = (isRange) =>
    52	        listPrice && (
    53	            <ListPrice
    54	                labelForA11y={labelForA11y}
    55	                currency={currency}
    56	                price={listPrice * quantity}
    57	                isRange={isRange}
    58	                {...listPriceProps}
    59	            />
    60	        )
    61	
    62	    const renderPriceSet = (isRange) => (
    63	        <>
    64	            {renderCurrentPrice(isRange)} {isOnSale && renderListPrice(isRange)}
    65	        </>
    66	    )
    67	
    68	    if (isASet) {
    69	        return renderCurrentPrice(true)
    70	    }
    71	
    72	    if (isMaster) {
    73	        return renderPriceSet(isRange)
    74	    }
    75	
    76	    return <Box>{renderPriceSet(false)}</Box>
    77	}

The actual merge is **not** in that function. It delegates to a private helper, `aggregateBonusProductQuantities`, at **`cart.js:78`**. That is where all the field handling lives.

## 2. What it merges, and on what key

`cart.js:573-586`:

```js
    productItems.forEach((item) => {
        if (item.bonusProductLineItem) {
            bonusProducts.push(item)
        } else {
            regularProducts.push(item)
        }
    })

    const consolidatedBonusProducts = aggregateBonusProductQuantities(bonusProducts)
```

- Only items with truthy `item.bonusProductLineItem` are candidates. Regular lines pass through byte-identical and are **reordered to the front**.
- Merge key is **`productId` alone**. Not `bonusDiscountLineItemId`, not `shipmentId`, not price, not `itemId`.

## 3. Exactly which numeric fields are summed / recomputed / carried over

The whole merge, `cart.js:78-98`:

```js
const aggregateBonusProductQuantities = (bonusItems) => {
    const productQuantityMap = new Map()

    bonusItems.forEach((item) => {
        const existingQuantity = productQuantityMap.get(item.productId) || 0
        productQuantityMap.set(item.productId, existingQuantity + (item.quantity || 0))
    })

    const result = []
    productQuantityMap.forEach((quantity, productId) => {
        const sampleItem = bonusItems.find((item) => item.productId === productId)
        if (sampleItem) {
            result.push({
                ...sampleItem,
                quantity: quantity
            })
        }
    })

    return result
}
```

`sampleItem` is `bonusItems.find(...)` — the **first** bonus line with that `productId`. The merged object is that first line spread wholesale, with exactly one key overwritten.

| Field | Treatment |
|---|---|
| `quantity` | **Summed** (`cart.js:83`), `\|\| 0` guard for missing |
| `price` | **Carried over unchanged from the first line.** Not summed, not recomputed |
| `basePrice` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `priceAfterItemDiscount` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `priceAfterOrderDiscount` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `pricePerUnit` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `adjustedTax` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `tax` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |
| `taxBasis` | Carried over unchanged from the first line |

Nothing is summed except `quantity`. Nothing is recomputed. There is no field-specific logic at all — the spread is blind, so any field you name that isn't `quantity` is first-line-wins.

**No.** `quantity` becomes `Σ qᵢ` while `price` stays `line₀.price` (which, per the house convention below, is line₀'s *line total*, i.e. `unit × q₀`). So on a merged item:

```
price / quantity  ==  (unit × q₀) / Σqᵢ     ≠  unit
```

Two bonus lines of qty 1 at unit 100 merge to `{quantity: 2, price: 100}` → `price/quantity = 50`. Under-reports by a factor of N for N equal-quantity lines.

**Severity caveat worth knowing before you act on this:** the canonical SFCC bonus line shape is all-zeros on money. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/mock-data.js:5739-5757` — `adjustedTax: 0, basePrice: 0, price: 0, priceAfterItemDiscount: 0, priceAfterOrderDiscount: 0, tax: 0, taxBasis: 0`, and **`pricePerUnit` is absent entirely**. It becomes a real wrong number only for a partially-discounted bonus product (percentage-off "choice of bonus"), where `price` is nonzero.

The upstream tests do not constrain this at all: across the entire describe block (`cart.test.js:1643-1990`) the string `price` appears **zero** times. No fixture even has a price field. 1:/**
2: * Selects the correct `getPriceData` result for the PDP given the current product, the cached
3: * master, and the active URL parameters.
4: *
5: * Extracted from the page's `useMemo` so the filtering and fallback logic is unit-testable
6: * without mounting a React component or mocking any hooks. The page's memo reduces to a
7: * single call:
8: *
9: *   `useMemo(() => selectVariantScopedPriceData(product, masterProductRef.current, urlPid, urlColour), [...])`
10: *
11: * Nothing else on the PDP ties URL params to a pricing result, and a mis-keyed filter here
12: * silently shows the wrong Was/Now — not a crash, not a blank, just wrong data. That is the
13: * failure mode `productInfo.ts`'s docblock describes for field mapping; the same reasoning
14: * applies here.
15: */
16:import { getPriceData } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
17:
18:/**
19: * A variant entry as this selector reads it.
20: * Only the two fields that drive the colour/pid filters are typed;
21: * everything else is spread into `getPriceData` unchanged.
22: */
23:export type ScopedVariant = {
24:  productId?: string;
25:  variationValues?: Record<string, string | undefined>;
26:  [key: string]: unknown;
27:};
28:
29:/**
30: * The subset of a product response this selector reads.
31: * Every field optional — absent fields are treated as absent, not as errors.
32: * Fields beyond this shape are spread into `getPriceData` unchanged.
33: */
34:export type ScopedProduct = {
35:  id?: string;
36:  master?: { masterId?: string };
37:  variants?: ScopedVariant[];
38:  tieredPrices?: unknown[];
39:  [key: string]: unknown;
40:};
41:
42:/**
43: * Returns the `getPriceData` result scoped to the variants that match the current URL
44: * selection, or `null` when no matching selection exists.
45: *
46: * @param product - The resolved product (master when colour-only; standalone variant when a
47: *   size is picked and `pid` is in the URL).
48: * @param cachedMaster - The last master product stored in `masterProductRef`, or `null`.
49: *   Used as the variant source when `product` has switched to a standalone variant that may
50: *   lack `tieredPrices`.
51: * @param urlPid - The `pid` URL parameter, if present.
52: * @param urlColour - The `color` URL parameter, if present.
53: */
54:export const selectVariantScopedPriceData = (
55:  product: ScopedProduct | null | undefined,
56:  cachedMaster: ScopedProduct | null,
57:  urlPid: string | undefined,
58:  urlColour: string | undefined,
59:) => {
60:  // ── Cached-master path (believed unreachable — see note below) ────────────────
61:  //
62:  // This path exists on the assumption that a standalone-variant SFCC response may lack
63:  // `variants[]`, requiring a cached master to supply them. However, `use-variation-
64:  // attributes.js:162` in the base app accesses `product.variants.filter(...)` completely
65:  // unguarded on every render. If any product type ever returned without `variants[]`, the
66:  // base PDP would throw on every size selection. It doesn't — so SFCC always populates
67:  // `variants[]`, and `product?.variants?.length` is always truthy on the next line. That
68:  // means `effectiveCachedMaster` is never consulted, and the deep-link fallback below it
69:  // never fires.
70:  //
71:  // The knock-on at the getPriceData call: when product is a variant (colour+size, pid in
72:  // URL), `getPriceData` ignores the injected `variants` array anyway — `findLowestPrice`
73:  // checks `type.master` and uses `[product]` for non-masters (product-utils.js:257). Was/Now
74:  // for the colour+size case comes from the variant's own `tieredPrices` (present because we
75:  // request `perPricebook:true`), not from the master variants we inject. The active path for
76:  // colour+size pricing is therefore the variant's own prices, regardless of this cache.
77:  //
78:  // Left in place pending a dev-org verification that variant responses always include
79:  // `variants[]`. Once confirmed, the `cachedMaster` parameter, `cachedMasterMatchesCurrent`,
80:  // `effectiveCachedMaster`, the deep-link fallback block, and the corresponding `useEffect`
81:  // + `masterProductRef` in `product-detail/index.tsx` can all be removed —
82:  // `masterVariants`/`masterProduct` would simply become `product.variants` and `product`.
83:  const cachedMasterMatchesCurrent =
84:    cachedMaster != null && (product?.id === cachedMaster.id || product?.master?.masterId === cachedMaster.id);
85:  const effectiveCachedMaster = cachedMasterMatchesCurrent ? cachedMaster : null;
86:
87:  const masterVariants = product?.variants?.length ? product.variants : effectiveCachedMaster?.variants;
88:  const masterProduct = product?.variants?.length ? product : effectiveCachedMaster;
89:
90:  // Deep-link fallback — see unreachability note above.
91:  if (!masterProduct || !masterVariants?.length) {
92:    if ((urlPid || urlColour) && product?.tieredPrices?.length) {
93:      return getPriceData(product);
94:    }
95:    return null;
96:  }
97:
98:  let matchingVariants: ScopedVariant[];
99:  if (urlPid) {
100:    const pidVariants = masterVariants.filter((v) => v.productId === urlPid);
101:    // Cross-check: if a colour is also selected, verify the pid variant belongs to it.
102:    //
103:    // When a shopper switches colour and the current size doesn't exist in the new colour,
104:    // `useVariant` matches nothing and the pid-rewriting effect bails out early
105:    // (`if (!variant) return`), leaving the URL with a stale pid still pointing at the
106:    // previous colour's variant. Using it unchecked would show the previous colour's
107:    // Was/Now price while the new colour is visually selected.
108:    //
109:    // If the pid variant's colour doesn't match urlColour (or the pid matched nothing),
110:    // fall back to colour-only pricing until the shopper picks a valid size in the new
111:    // colour and the pid is correctly rewritten.
112:    const pidColour = pidVariants[0]?.variationValues?.color;
113:    const pidIsStale = urlColour && (pidVariants.length === 0 || pidColour !== urlColour);
114:    matchingVariants = pidIsStale ? masterVariants.filter((v) => v.variationValues?.color === urlColour) : pidVariants;
115:  } else if (urlColour) {
116:    // Colour selected, size not yet — price spans all sizes for this colour
117:    matchingVariants = masterVariants.filter((v) => v.variationValues?.color === urlColour);
118:  } else {
119:    return null; // no selection yet
120:  }
121:
122:  if (!matchingVariants.length) return null;
123:  return getPriceData({ ...masterProduct, variants: matchingVariants });
124:};

########## pricing-currency-globale.md ##########
7:Scope: price feeds & pricebooks, price display & tax, sale & markdown pricing, multi-currency & FX, VIC/customer-group pricing, and Global-e pricing & cart handoff. The promotions engine (coupons, stacking) lives in [promotions.md](promotions.md).
13:## 1. Price Feeds & Pricebooks (PRC-01 – PRC-04, PRC-34 – PRC-35)
15:- Product pricing consumed from AP21 via MuleSoft, including current selling price, original/RRP price, and markdown status. Mapped to SFCC pricebook fields (PRC-01, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma; assumption is RetailPrice stored as an additional price field; EK query outstanding on who owns final RetailPrice functional confirmation)
17:- **Base RRP pricebooks per currency** (minimum: AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) consumed from AP21 via MuleSoft into SFCC — source of truth for domestic prices and calculation base for FX-derived international markets (PRC-34, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
19:- Future-dated markdown pricing activation via MuleSoft — date and time supported (not date only), so sale pricing can go live at a precise datetime. Confirmed 2026-06-24 (RJ/Mani, based on Billy's AP21 feedback). Timezone mapping: one default timezone per storefront; times in local pricebooks are expressed in the storefront's timezone; MuleSoft is responsible for converting and setting the appropriate time in SFCC (PRC-03, confirmed — signed off by Emma/Rebecca 2026-06-24)
20:- Pricebooks for multiple currencies per regional site (PRC-04, confirmed — signed off by Dani + Emma)
35:- Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, and order history. Note (DR): sale items are usually excluded from recommendations via a manual rule (PRC-09)
43:## 4. Multi-Currency & Regional Pricebooks (PRC-14, PRC-36 – PRC-43, PRC-47 – PRC-52)
47:- Per currency, the system stores the **conversion approach**: (a) Base RRP, (b) Fixed Pricelist from AP21, (c) Fixed FX rate from base, or (d) Dynamic FX rate from base (PRC-37)
49:- Pricebooks generated from Global-e pricing data and imported into SFCC (PRC-39)
50:- Target-currency price calculation: `base pricebook price × FX rate × country coefficient × product-class coefficient` (PRC-40)
55:- **Currency rounding strategy** per currency (e.g. nearest whole AED, 2 decimal EUR, 0 decimal JPY); applied at line-item level before tax/promotion stacking (PRC-49)
73:- **Customer group discounts do NOT stack on sale items** (PRC-18, revised per DR): sale items are excluded from promotion set-ups. Example: a Gold VIC customer receives 10% off full-price items, but if they add a sale product to cart they get the sale price only — no extra 10% on top. The system must continue to support this exclusion.

| `imageGroups` @ `viewType: 'swatch'`, hardcoded `color` | **[P]** | `use-variation-attributes.js:26-34` |
| **`product.variants.filter(...)` — unguarded** | **[P]** | **`use-variation-attributes.js:75`** |
| `c_maxOrderQuantity` | **[P]** custom | `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts:52`, called at `product-item/index.tsx:363` and `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:304` |
| `productId` \|\| `id` (testid) | **[B]**/**[P]** | `product-item/index.tsx:320` |
| `bonusProductLineItem` | **[B]** | `product-item/index.tsx:344,349,356,357` |

Plus `cartItemMapper.ts` (called at `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:292`): `imageGroups`+`variationValues` (`:93-96`), `images[0].disBaseLink/.link/.alt` (`:99-100`), `productName`/`name` (`:100,135`), `variationAttributes` (`:122`), `itemId`/`productId` (`:133-134`), `quantity` (`:138`), `stepQuantity` (`:139`).

---

# (b) READ but NOT covered by the projection

Ordered by severity.

### 1. `variants` (+ `variants[].variationValues`, `variants[].orderable`, `variants[].productId`) — **hard crash**
`use-variation-attributes.js:75` is `return product.variants.filter(...)` — **no optional chaining**. It is called once per variation value from the `useMemo` at `:132-167`, which iterates `product.variationAttributes`. The projection selects `variationAttributes` but **not** `variants`, so for every cart line with variation attributes this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')`, taking down the whole drawer render.

This is not speculative: the cart drawer renders today with a populated colour/size line (`item-attributes.tsx:31` cites real "Lilac Sand, One size" data), which means `variationAttributes` is non-empty today, which means that same unguarded line already executes today without throwing — so `variants` is present in today's response and the `select` string is what removes it.

### 2. `variationValues` — wrong image + empty attribute line
Not in the projection. **[P]**-only (proven by the `ProductItem` type dump above and `cartItemMapper.ts:36-39`). Readers: `item-image.tsx:100` / base `:28`, `item-attributes.tsx:98` / base `:53`, `cartItemMapper.ts:95,122`, `use-variation-params.js:24,46`.

Combined with the PR's `allImages: true` — which is exactly the flag that makes SCAPI return the *whole* image model rather than only the requested variant's images — that means the first colour in the master's image model, not the shopper's colour. Note base's own cart pairs `allImages: true` with **no `select`** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:158-176`), i.e. `variationValues` present — that is the coherent combination this PR breaks.

The override renders `Object.values({}).join(', ')` → an **empty `<Text>`** (`item-attributes.tsx:149`), and `cartItemMapper.selectCombinedAttributes` returns `''` (`:123`). The Figma "Lilac Sand, One size" line disappears.

Minimal fix: add `variationValues` to the projection (preferred, matches base), **or** drop `allImages: true`.

### 3. `inventory.stockLevel`, `inventory.lowestStockLevelProductName`, `inventories[]` — inventory message goes permanently dead
Read at `use-derived-product.js:18-22,37,43,82-88`; rendered at `product-item/index.tsx:399-407`. Killed **twice over**: dropped from `expand` (no `availability`) *and* absent from the `select`. `stockLevel` falls to `0` (`:37`) → `isOutOfStock` true (`:72`) → but `showInventoryMessage` (`:122-124`) also needs `variant || type.bundle || type.item`, and all three collapse to falsy under this projection, so the net effect is silence rather than a false "Out of stock". ### 4. `c_maxOrderQuantity` — defeats the whole purpose of `maxOrderQuantity.ts`
Read at `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts:52`; drives the stepper `max` (`product-item/index.tsx:363`) and the "Maximum purchase quantity reached" message (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:304`). Not in the projection → permanently falls back to `3`. That file's docblock (`:19-23`) states the design intent explicitly: it "picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships, with no further frontend change needed". This projection silently removes that property.

### 5. `stepQuantity`
`use-derived-product.js:38`, `cartItemMapper.ts:139`. Falls to `1`. No visible impact in the cart drawer today (`ProductItem` destructures only `showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity` at `:293`, and `ZimmQuantityStepper` uses `min={1}`), but it is a genuine read that goes silently wrong.

### 6. `minOrderQuantity`
`use-derived-product.js:39-40`. Only matters when `quantity` is falsy, which the merge guarantees it isn't (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:276`). Low impact.

### 7. `type.item` and `type.variant`
The projection has `type.(bundle,master,set)` only. `type.item` is read at `use-derived-product.js:51` (feeds `isOutOfStock` `:72-77` and `showInventoryMessage` `:123`); `type.variant` at `use-variation-attributes.js:114` (only under `isProductPartOfBundle`, which is `false` here). **Add `item` and `variant` to `type.(...)` — it costs nothing.**

### 8. `imageGroups[viewType=swatch]`
`getVariantValueSwatch` (`use-variation-attributes.js:26-34`) requests `viewType: 'swatch'`; the `[viewType=small]` predicate strips it, so every decorated value's `image` becomes `undefined`. Latent only — nothing in the cart drawer renders those swatches (`ProductItem` never destructures `variationAttributes` from `useDerivedProduct`).

### 9. `pricePerUnit` — base-only
Base `item-price.jsx:55,77,98` reads it; the override deleted `PricePerItem` (`item-price.tsx:39-46`). Since every path in this repo resolves to the override, this is not a live break — but note it also needs the `prices` expand, so it is doubly removed.

`getPriceData`/`findLowestPrice` (`product-utils.js:123-169,246-283`) read `hitType`, `variants[].price`, `productPromotions[].promotionalPrice`, `tieredPrices[].price/.quantity`, `priceMax`, `variants.length`. Only reached when `variant.itemId` is falsy (`item-price.tsx:94`), which never happens for a basket line. Safe **for this call site**; would break if this `select` were ever copied to the wishlist fetch.

---

# (c) Projection entries nothing reads (dead selection)

Genuinely dead:

1. **`variationAttributes.(... name ...)` — dead for the cart drawer specifically.** `getDisplayVariationValues` uses `attribute.name` as the object **key** (`product-utils.js:44`), and the cart's override throws the keys away: `Object.values(variationValues).join(', ')` (`item-attributes.tsx:149`, reached because `product-item/index.tsx:342` passes `combineAttributeValues`). The keys are only used on the non-combined path (`:156`), which base callers of the same component do use. **Keep it** unless you are certain no other surface renders labelled attributes — it is cheap.
2. **`imageGroups[...].variationAttributes.(id,values.(value))` — 100% dead *as configured*.** `findImageGroupBy` only touches these when `selectedVariationAttributes` is non-empty (`image-groups-utils.js:38-58`), and with `variationValues` missing it is always `{}`. So this sub-selection is paid for and never used. The fix is to add `variationValues`, not to remove this.
3. **`c_isSale` — selected but almost certainly unreachable.** Read at `item-image.tsx:108` / base `:35`. Custom attributes need the `custom_properties` expand in this codebase's own practice: `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:50` (`expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`) and `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:318`. `expand: ['images','variations']` omits it, so `c_isSale` (and `c_maxOrderQuantity`) will not come back regardless of the `select`. Note also that `"custom_properties"` is **not** in the generated `expand` union (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:57374`), so adding it to a typed TS call site will need a cast — base gets away with it only because those files are `.jsx`.

Everything else in the projection is genuinely read: `id` (`item-name.tsx:74`, `item-attributes.tsx:131`, `product-item/index.tsx:320`), `name` (`item-name.tsx:79`, `item-price.tsx:140,150`, `cartItemMapper.ts:100,135`), `master.masterId` (`item-name.tsx:74`, `item-image.tsx:95`), `type.bundle` (`item-attributes.tsx:110,136`, `use-derived-product.js:36`), `type.master`/`type.set` (`item-price.tsx:88-89`), `variationAttributes.(id, values.(value))` (`product-utils.js:31,36`), `imageGroups[].viewType` (`image-groups-utils.js:22`), `images.(link,disBaseLink,alt)` (`item-image.tsx:147-148`).

---

# On `expand`

Removing `prices`, `promotions`, `availability`, `bundled_products`, `options`, `links` from the default set:

- **`prices` → removes `price`, `pricePerUnit`, `priceMax`, `priceRanges`, `prices`, `tieredPrices`.** Safe for the cart drawer: the merge re-asserts `price: item.price` **after** `...fullProduct` (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:275`), so the catalog `price` was already being discarded; `getPriceData`/`findLowestPrice` (the only `tieredPrices`/`priceMax` readers) are unreachable because `variant.itemId` is truthy (`item-price.tsx:94`); and the override deleted the only `pricePerUnit` reader. **But `perPricebook: true` (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:479`) becomes a dead parameter** — it exists to return the per-price-book `prices` map, which both the expand removal and the `select` drop. Remove it in the same PR or keep `prices`.
- **`promotions` → removes `productPromotions`.** Safe: the only reader is `findLowestPrice` (`product-utils.js:261`), unreachable as above. The promo pill in `item-attributes` uses basket `priceAdjustments[].promotionId` + a separate `usePromotions` call (`item-attributes.tsx:80,87-96`), untouched.
- **`availability` → removes `inventory`/`inventories`. NOT safe** — see (b)(3). Base's own precedent is instructive: the one place base uses a `select` at all, it pairs it with an expand that covers what it selects — `expand: ['availability','variations'], select: '(data.(id,inventory,inventories,master))'` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:196-197`, and identically at `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:173-174`).
- **`custom_properties` → never in the default set either, and needed for `c_isSale`/`c_maxOrderQuantity`.** See (c)(3).
- **`bundled_products` → removes `bundledProducts`.** Read at `item-attributes.tsx:182` — but only on the wishlist branch (`!productBundleIds`), and from that file's **own** `useProduct` call, not this fetch. No impact here.
- **`options`, `links`** — no readers found in this path.

## One unverified syntax risk

`imageGroups[viewType=small]` is an attribute-predicate filter. There is **no precedent for it anywhere in base retail-react-app 10.0.0 or this repo** — every existing `select` is plain parenthesis projection (`'(data.(id,inventory,inventories,master))'`, `pages/cart/index.jsx:197` and `pages/product-detail/index.jsx:174`), and the repo has zero occurrences of `imageGroups[` in any `select` (grep-confirmed). I could not verify from the codebase that SCAPI's `select` grammar accepts a value predicate rather than an index. Worth an actual live probe against the sandbox before merge — if the predicate is rejected, the endpoint will either 400 or silently return no image groups at all.

## Suggested minimal correction to the projection

```
(data.(id,name,master.(masterId),type.(bundle,item,master,set,variant),c_isSale,c_maxOrderQuantity,
```

     8	/**
     9	 * Find the ImageGroup that matches the criteria supplied
    10	 *
    11	 * @param {Object} imageGroups - The product/variations image groups you want to search.
    12	 * @param {Object} options - Search criteria to match on the ImageGroup object.
    13	 * @param {string} options.viewType - Typically this refers to image sizes like small, medium, large. But can vary based on your back-end configuration.
    14	 * @param {Object} options.selectedVariationAttributes - A key/value object consisting of attibute id's and their values.
    15	 * @returns {Object} - The ImageGroup matching the search criteria
    16	 */
    17	export const findImageGroupBy = (imageGroups = [], options) => {
    18	    let {viewType, selectedVariationAttributes = {}} = options
    19	
    20	    // Start by filtering out any imageGroup that isn't the correct viewType.
    21	    imageGroups = imageGroups.filter(
    22	        ({viewType: imageGroupViewType}) => imageGroupViewType === viewType
    23	    )
    24	
    25	    // Not all variation attributes are reflected in images. For example, you probably
    26	    // won't have a separate image group for various sizes, but you might for colors. For that
    27	    // reason we need to know what are valid attribute values to filter on.
    28	    const refinableAttributeIds = [
    29	        ...new Set(
    30	            imageGroups
    31	                .reduce((acc, {variationAttributes = []}) => [...acc, ...variationAttributes], [])
    32	                .map(({id}) => id)
    33	        )
    34	    ]
    35	
    36	    // Update the `selectedVariationAttributes` by filtering out the attributes that have no
    37	    // representation in this imageGroup.
    38	    selectedVariationAttributes = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes).reduce((acc, curr) => {
    39	        return refinableAttributeIds.includes(curr)
    40	            ? {
    41	                  ...acc,
    42	                  [`${curr}`]: selectedVariationAttributes[curr]
    43	              }
    44	            : acc
    45	    }, {})
    46	
    47	    // Find the image group that has all the all the selected variation value attributes.
    48	    imageGroups = imageGroups.find(({variationAttributes = []}) => {
    49	        const selectedIds = Object.keys(selectedVariationAttributes)
    50	
    51	        return selectedIds.every((selectedId) => {
    52	            const selectedValue = selectedVariationAttributes[selectedId]
    53	
    54	            return variationAttributes.find(
    55	                ({id, values}) =>
    56	                    id === selectedId && values.every(({value}) => value === selectedValue)
    57	            )
    58	        })
    59	    })
    60	
    61	    return imageGroups
    62	}

content.text:
All claims verified from source. Here are the findings.

## Ground truth established first

`ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts:6968`, docs at `:6910-6966`):

| field | meaning | unit or line? |
|---|---|---|
| `basePrice` | "the **unit price** not including adjustments" (`:6914`) | **unit** |
| `price` | "price of the **line item** before applying any adjustments" (`:6935`) | **line total** |
| `priceAfterItemDiscount` | "price of the product **line item** including item-level adjustments" | **line total** |
| `priceAfterOrderDiscount` | "…including item-level adjustments and prorated order-level adjustments" | **line total** |
| `pricePerUnit` | **not a member of `ProductItem` at all** | — |

Corroborated by fixture `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/mocks/mock-data.js:37-55`: `basePrice: 9.59`, `quantity: 2`, `price: 19.18`, `priceAfterItemDiscount: 19.18`, `priceAfterOrderDiscount: 19.18`. So `price === basePrice × quantity`, and "adjustments" means `priceAdjustments` (promotions) only.

`pricePerUnit` exists only on Shopper **Products** `Product` (`:32760`, field `:32782`), documented "The price per unit if defined for the product", and fixtures show it equals the product's current unit price (`standard-product.js:78-79` `price: 4, pricePerUnit: 4`; `product-bundle.js:200-201` `price: 54.99, pricePerUnit: 54.99`).

---

## Findings

**1. `item-price.tsx:61-78` — order-level discounts are rendered as a per-line "Was/Now" markdown, and the same discount is then subtracted again in the Subtotal block.** 

`effectiveCurrentPrice = priceAfterOrderDiscount ?? …`, `isOnSale = price > effectiveCurrentPrice`, `listPrice = isOnSale ? price : null`.

Inputs: 1 unit @ $1000, no item promo, VIC 20% order promo. SCAPI returns `price: 1000`, `priceAfterItemDiscount: 1000`, `priceAfterOrderDiscount: 800`, `productSubTotal: 1000`, `orderPriceAdjustments: [{itemText:'VIC 20%', price:-200}]`.

Output, all inside one panel: line item reads **"Was $1,000.00 Now $800.00"** (`item-price.tsx:104-108`); Subtotal reads **$1,000.00** (`order-summary/index.tsx:218`); then **"VIC 20% Applied −$200.00"** (`:226-248`). The line item claims $800 while the Subtotal directly below claims $1,000, and the discount is visually applied twice. Base avoided this precisely by using `priceAfterItemDiscount`, which reconciles exactly with `productSubTotal` — "including item-level adjustments, but **not** including order-level adjustments" (`index.cjs.d.ts:7040`).

Requirements angle: PRC-09 (`.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:35`) asks for "Original list price displayed alongside active sale price" — a markdown concept. PRC-18 (`:73`) treats customer-group discounts as a separate mechanism that explicitly does not stack with sale. Rendering a member discount as a strikethrough conflates the two. **Confidence: high** on the mechanism and the arithmetic; the product call on whether that's wanted is yours.

**2. `item-price.tsx:62,70` — the one case PRC-09 actually asks for, a sale/markdown pricebook, still gets no Was/Now.**

`price` is the *pricebook-resolved* line price, so for a markdown with no promotion attached, `price === priceAfterItemDiscount === priceAfterOrderDiscount` → `isOnSale` false → `listPrice: null` → no strikethrough. PRC-01 (`:15`) states the original/RRP arrives as a *separate additional price field* — which is exactly what the base comment it deletes ("listPrice is not available via basket pricing") meant. The override reverses that comment without making `listPrice` available; it substitutes "pre-promotion line price", a different quantity. Net effect: Was/Now fires for promotions (where PRC-18's model says it shouldn't) and stays silent for markdowns (where PRC-09 says it should). Contrast `getPriceData` (`product-utils.js:139-144`), which derives a genuine `listPrice` from `tieredPrices` — product data the basket doesn't carry, and which this PR's projection also drops. **Confidence: high.**

**3. `item-price.tsx:74` — the per-unit division is unnecessary for the pre-discount case and lossy for the post-discount case.**

`basePrice` is already the unit price, on the basket item, no division needed — base's own `PricePerItem` prop is even *named* `basePrice` (`item-price.jsx:19,22,34`) while being fed `pricePerUnit`. For a *post*-order-discount unit price there is no SCAPI field, so division is the only route, but it doesn't round-trip: qty 3, `price: 100.00`, 20% order discount → `priceAfterOrderDiscount: 80.00` → `80/3 = 26.6666…` → renders **"$26.67ea"** beside **"Now $80.00"**; 3 × 26.67 = 80.01. PRC-49 (`:55`) specifies rounding applied at line-item level. **Confidence: high.**
